scope: Engine-light platform services: a closed capability set (entitlement, achievement, leaderboard, cloud_save, identity), a provider descriptor built by explicit registration that declares which capabilities a given vendor provider supports so a composition fails closed at compose time when a required capability is missing, typed intents (check_entitlement, unlock, report_score, read_leaderboard, cloud_write, cloud_read) applied to an immutable state with deterministic replay and stable failure codes for not_entitled, offline, rate_limited, capability.unsupported, and identity.missing, and an offline pending-write queue keyed by idempotency keys that replays in order, with a thin Unity adapter planned separately behind one provider interface over the Meta Horizon Platform SDK, the PICO platform SDK, Steamworks, Apple Game Center and StoreKit, and Unity Gaming Services Cloud Save, with an entitlement gate at boot that fails closed

sources.admitted_role: Primary platform evidence that a store-issued entitlement check is a boot-time, request/response call against the signed-in account, returning a definite entitled/not-entitled result rather than a locally cached assumption

Account identity and sign-in status are a Settings-adjacent display concern, for example a signed-in-as row on a settings screen reading this family's identity capability; the Settings definition/profile/applicator model itself is not re-derived here and contributes no evidence for this family's semantics

Ranks platform services thirteenth and records that every shipped shape needs entitlement, and most need achievements, leaderboards, or cloud save; this is the motivating gap the queue candidate answers, not evidence for the common kernel

States that a package manifest or one successful profile does not prove other Unity, provider SDK, store, or account tuples; this family's Unity-adapter admitted role for every vendor SDK source is bounded by that policy rather than by the vendor's own text

source_gate_non_claims: No source grants package maturity, release, certification, store approval, platform review outcome, or device authority

The first implementation is a capability, provider-descriptor, intent, immutable-state, and offline-queue substrate; it is not a store integration, a storefront, or a purchasing flow, and admits no claim that any named store, platform, or SDK version is installed, configured, or certified

The family guarantees the plumbing only: that an accepted check_entitlement, unlock, report_score, read_leaderboard, cloud_write, or cloud_read intent reached the injectable provider port with the exact capability, payload, and idempotency key it computed; whether a real store granted entitlement, unlocked an achievement, accepted a score, or accepted a cloud write is a human or process observation recorded outside package claims

Store approval, real entitlement, and real leaderboard behaviour are receipts from a real store build on a device, never package claims, and no test in this family's gates claims a store granted entitlement, unlocked an achievement, accepted a score, or persisted a cloud file

Automated or device evidence recorded for one provider, store, or account tuple never transfers to another provider, store, platform, or account, and a capability proven available on one provider is never assumed on another
